correctness.rationale: For p odd away from D, the residue order ρ of x=α/β controls the U zeros and divides p−χ by Frobenius; odd-prime lifting gives the U rank tower. A V zero occurs precisely at an odd multiple of t=ρ/2 when ρ is even, with initial valuation equal to ν_p(U_ρ); for odd ρ there is no V zero. At p|D one has p≥5 and ν_p(x−1)=ν_p(D)/2>1/(p−1), so the binomial lifting argument works in the local splitting field, which need not itself be ramified. This gives ν_p(U_n)=ν_p(n), while the reduced V trace is nonzero. Inverting a divisor indicator gives a delta, so the U local-part telescoping coefficients are nonnegative and the V odd-multiple condition gives paired positive and negative towers at t p^j and 2t p^j. At the j=1 index, cancellation gives the necessary p-free rank divisibility r|k(p−1); the whole tower satisfies it conversely. The ramified U tower needs p. For inert primes x^( (p+1)/2 )=(−1)^((p+3)/2); with ρ>2 this gives exactly the two character tests. At 2, even P gives ν₂(V_n)=ν₂(P) for odd n and 1 for even n. For odd P, the zero indices modulo 2 are multiples of 3, with ν₂(U₃)=1 and ν₂(V₃)=2. Odd powers preserve these valuations and doubling uses V_{2j}=V_j²−2(−1)^j and U_{2j}=U_jV_j. This gives the listed factors, including the negative V transform at 6 for odd P and at 2 when ν₂(P)>1, and the constant V cases are realizable. For nonsquareness use D=5 at P=1, and P²<D<(P+1)² for P≥2. The real quadratic field is distinct from Q(i), so the joint sign classes have relative prime density 1/4, giving 1/2 and 3/4 as claimed. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; the recorded range of 280 parameter-prime pairs and n≤200 does not prove the all-index or density results.

evidence: Murru–Sanna Theorem 1.5 gives the rank valuation for arbitrary Lucas parameters in scope, including the p≥5 discriminant-prime valuation ν_p(U_n)=ν_p(n) on the rank and explicit ν₂(U₃) and ν₂(U₆) dependence off an even discriminant.
The split companion result assumes square positive discriminant and integral roots; the global Dold survey is not a prime-part classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Valuation formulas alone are not a Dold theorem. Here they mechanically give the only parity-dependent input needed for the earlier repair argument: if P is odd, τ(2)=3, U₃=P²+1 and U₆=U₃·P(P²+3) give valuations 1 and 3, respectively. Thus A₂ is literally the classical Fibonacci A₂ sequence. The discriminant-prime simplification is also explicitly contained in the older valuation theorem.

value.rationale: A complete local repair and sign classification is a meaningful target. Here the distinguishing uniformity combines already available companion classifications with a first-kind proof whose odd-prime part needs no parity condition and whose remaining dyadic case is exactly the known Fibonacci sequence. The synthesis is useful exposition, but no independently useful unknown exact fact remains as the stated contribution.
